for, taken or turned away by the storage host. The server asks the bucket
and answers `confirmed` (the file is there and counts against the person's

get.summary:
One creator's live content, to ANYBODY.

WHY IT HAD TO EXIST. A shared store link (build brief C3) opens a
creator's shop with no session. The only per-creator content read was
GET /users/:wawuId/content, which sits on a guarded controller and 401s
an anonymous caller, so the store rendered identity and cross-sell over
an empty shelf: the page whose entire job is to sell somebody's work
could not show any of it. The alternative considered and rejected was
filling the shelf from /content/public/featured, which is
platform-wide - that would present an arbitrary subset of the platform
as one person's shop.

WHY IT IS SAFE. `listByCreator` already takes an OPTIONAL requester and
`resolveUnlockedSet(undefined, ...)` returns an empty set, so every
piece comes back locked and `fullAssetUrl` is withheld from all of them.
An anonymous caller therefore sees exactly what a signed-in stranger
sees: titles, covers, prices, and nothing behind the paywall. It also
filters `status: 'live'`, so a pending or rejected piece is never
exposed.

It lives on this ungated controller rather than as a bypass on the
guarded one, which is the same call this file's header comment makes
about `featured`: weakening a class-level guard for one route is how a
guard stops meaning anything.

reads it from `GET /money/transfers/{id}`. The account is name-checked

confirms them by saving the account again. A withdrawal to the payout
account while its holder is not the person's verified name is `409

to anyone else's account is unchanged. Asking the bank about an account
that is not saved, with a name token the person did not get for it, is a

past them, before the PIN, the bank not asked). The same Idempotency-Key and

the PIN; limit_reached (WAWU's limit or the provider's, WALLET-23) before

post.summary:
Turns points into cash in the wallet, once. The cash is worked out at the
config's rate and rounded down; the points are held (soonest-ending lots
first) and the cash is paid from WAWU's own account into the person's
wallet; the points are spent only when the provider has confirmed it, and
go back to their lots if it did not move. Answers 201 with the
conversion: `completed`, `pending` while the provider has not confirmed
the cash yet (the points stay on hold; poll `GET /points/convert/{id}`;
it is never sent again), or `failed` when the cash did not move and the
points are back. The same Idempotency-Key and body answer the first
result again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) without checking the PIN.
The body carries the `quoteToken` of the quote the person was shown: the
conversion is paid at that quote or not at all. If the rate, the
minimum, the cap or the cash changed since (or the token is not this
person's, not for these points, or past its end), it is `409
quote_changed` with the new quote in `reason.pointsQuote`, and nothing
is paid. A body with no token is a plain 400.
Before the PIN, and changing nothing: `422 below_minimum`, `402
insufficient_points`, `400 amount_out_of_range` (more than one move
carries), `409 quote_changed`, `409 currency_not_supported`, `409
wallet_not_open`, `503 fees_not_set`.

the signed quote `POST /points/shortfall` sends back. Holds nothing and
takes nothing: a 200, whatever it says. A tool that is not in the plan,
or a count that is not a whole number above zero, is a 400.

post.summary:
Buys exactly the shortfall of one job from the wallet, once (PT3). The
body is the job as it was quoted plus `wallet.payment.totalKobo` and
`wallet.payment.quoteToken`; the PIN is in `X-Transaction-Pin`. One
lot of the shortfall's points is added when the provider confirms the
debit, ending after the bought-points expiry. Answers 201 with the
purchase: `paid`, `pending` while the provider has not confirmed (poll
`GET /points/shortfall/{id}`; it is never sent again) or `failed` when
nothing moved. The same Idempotency-Key and body answer the first result
again (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) without checking the PIN. Refused with
nothing taken and the key given back: `422 points_cap_reached` (buying points would not
let the job run), `409 points_not_short` (the person has enough now),
`409 quote_changed` with the new quote (the balance, the rate or the
expiry moved), `409 wallet_not_open`.

post.summary:
Starts a VoiceOver job (PT2): `text`, a `voiceId` from the list and the
`quoteToken` of the `POST /points/quote` the person saw. Holds the job's
points, answers `202` with the job `working` and makes the audio after the
answer; `GET /ai-tools/jobs/{id}` is what the app polls. The points are
kept only when the audio is made and given back when it is not.

Needs an `Idempotency-Key` (8 to 128 of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`): the same key and
words again answer the first job (`200`, `Idempotent-Replayed: true`)
and hold nothing more; the same key with other words is `409
idempotency_key_reused`. Refused with nothing held: `422
points_cap_reached` naming the cap (characters, minutes or the day's
points), `402 insufficient_points`, `409 quote_changed` (the cost is not
what the quote showed), `400 ai_voice_unknown`, `503 ai_tool_unavailable`.
A refusal leaves the key free to use once the cause is fixed.

whatever the length. The request, the answer, the `Idempotency-Key` rule
and the refusals are those of `POST /ai-tools/voiceover/jobs`, plus

limit, and `400 ai_prompt_empty`. Nothing is held when a job is refused.

the person uploaded. The Hub reads the file's length itself and prices the
minutes from that, so the phone sends no length. Answers the same quote

`422 ai_file_unreadable`; over the longest job the quote's `cap` names
`minutes_per_job` and `canRun` is false.

recording or video the person uploaded (`POST /uploads/presign`, folder
`ai/input-audio` or `ai/input-video`, then `POST /uploads/confirm`), an

subtitle file (`subtitles`, SRT). The request, the answer and the
`Idempotency-Key` rule are those of `POST /ai-tools/voiceover/jobs`, plus
`404 not_found` (not the caller's own file), `422 ai_file_too_large` and
`422 ai_file_unreadable`, each with nothing held; over the longest job the
answer is `422 points_cap_reached` naming `minutes_per_job`. The uploaded
file is deleted when the job ends, either way.

get.summary: The offer open for registration.

429.description: `reason.code` `referral_attempts_limited`: this address tried too many codes we do not have; wait a few minutes. (The plain rate limit has no `reason`.)

get.summary:
Before paying: does this referral code apply, and what would the person
pay. Never the limit, the count or the community. A code we do not have
is a 404 `referral_unknown`. Advice only: the registration decides again.
An address that has tried too many codes we do not have is asked to wait
(429 `referral_attempts_limited`).

200.description: Exactly one of `flutterwaveConfig` and `completed` is present. `flutterwaveConfig` (open the checkout with it) comes whenever `amountKobo` is above 0. `completed` comes instead when `amountKobo` is 0 (a free referral code): the registration is already paid and there is nothing to pay.

400.description: `reason.code` `phone_invalid`, `email_invalid`, `name_invalid` or `consent_required`; a malformed body has no `reason`.

404.description: `reason.code` `no_open_offer` (no offer has this id) or `referral_unknown` (no such referral code).

409.description: `reason.code` `offer_closed` (closed or not open yet) or `already_registered` (this phone or email already paid; nothing is charged).

429.description: `reason.code` `referral_attempts_limited`: this address tried too many codes we do not have, and a registration that carries a code waits; one with no code is not refused by it. (The plain rate limit has no `reason`.)

post.summary:
Register and get the checkout settings. Every call that passes the checks
adds a new registration with a new reference, even for the same offer,
phone and email, so each checkout has its own reference.
Nothing is charged here: the payment happens in the Flutterwave checkout
with the answer's `flutterwaveConfig`, and counts only after
POST /waitlist/registrations/verify (or Flutterwave's own notice).

With a `referralCode` (REF-01) the answer also carries `referral`. A code
at price 0 needs no checkout: the answer has `completed` and no
`flutterwaveConfig`, and the registration is already paid.

409.description: `reason.code` `payment_not_confirmed` (Flutterwave does not say it succeeded yet: check again, never pay again), `transaction_already_used` or `already_registered`.

422.description: `reason.code` `payment_mismatch`: the payment is not this registration's (amount, currency or reference).

503.description: `reason.code` `payment_check_unavailable`: Flutterwave could not be reached; try the check again.

post.summary:
Confirm a payment. The server asks Flutterwave itself (succeeded, this
registration's reference, naira, not less than the fee) before it marks
the registration paid, so the transaction id is only a claim. Idempotent:
a paid registration answers the same result again.

404.description: `reason.code` `not_found`: the same answer for a reference that does not exist and one that was never issued.

get.summary: Where a registration stands: status and first name only, never a phone or email.

400.description: `reason.code` `code_invalid`: not 8 letters and numbers. A malformed body has no `reason`.

404.description: `reason.code` `code_not_found`: the same answer for a code that does not exist, is not paid, or is not tied to a phone or email the caller has proven.

409.description: `reason.code` `contact_not_verified` (the account has no proven phone or email), `code_refunded` (an extra payment being refunded), `already_claimed` (by another account), `offer_unavailable`, or `claimed_by_you` (only for a claim made before its answer was kept; the same account asking again is otherwise answered 200).

post.summary:
Claim a paid registration with its launch access code. The caller must
hold the registration's phone or email, proven to WAWU ID; the code alone
is never enough. Gives what the registration's plan gives, its days
counted from now, once. The account that made the claim and sends the
same code again is answered with the same plan (a 200, nothing granted
twice), so an answer that was lost on the way can be asked for again.

info.title: WAWU Hub API
info.description:
The contract the WAWU web client generates its types from.

ENVELOPE: every successful response is wrapped by ResponseInterceptor
before it leaves the server. The schemas below describe the INNER
payload, which is what a client sees after unwrapping:

  plain      {statusCode, message, data: <schema>}
  paginated  {statusCode, message, data: <schema>[],
              pagination: {currentPage, nextPage, perPage, total}}

The web client unwraps in apiFetch/apiFetchPaginated (src/lib/api/client.ts),
so generated types intentionally describe the inner payload, not the envelope.

priceKobo.description: Price per message in kobo. Required when `enabled` is true and none is saved yet.

responseHours.description: Hours the creator has to reply. Left out means unchanged.

enabled.description: Whether fans may send paid messages.

amount.description: Whole naira, like every other amount in this codebase.

bankCode.description: A bank CODE ("044"), never a bank name. Transfers cannot use a name.

accountNumber.description: NUBAN. Ten digits in Nigeria, and never anything but digits.

extension.description: File extension without the dot. Sanitised again server-side.

contentLength.description:
Exact byte length of the file. The presigned URL is signed FOR this
length, so storage rejects an upload of any other size — previously the
only cap was client-side and trivially bypassed by calling the presigned
URL directly.

format.description:
Optional, ME-04: the content format the file is for (`video`, `pdf`...).
Only for `content/full` and `content/preview`. Naming one adds that
format's rules (GET /uploads/formats) to the checks below: the types it
takes in that folder and its own size cap. Left out, the call is checked
exactly as before.

tierState.description:
The person's tier: `none` (never had one), `active`, `ending` or `ended`.
`tier_required` answers `none` or `ended`.

productsAllowed.description: Products they may have published at once (0 when nothing allows publishing).

currency.description:
The currency of every amount in `tiers` and `extraProducts`. The offers
(`currency`, `tiers`, `extraProducts`) are always there; they are absent
only when the Hub could not read the plan at that moment, and the app
then shows `message` alone.

tiers.description:
The tiers that would let the person publish another, in both refusals:
once bought they leave more places than the person has products
published now (the extras they hold carry over). For `tier_required`
that is every tier for someone with nothing published, and only the big
enough ones for someone who still has products up after a tick or tier
ended. For `product_limit_reached` it is the tiers above the one they
hold. The list is empty when no tier does (they hold the top one, or they
have more published than any tier allows); `message` then says products
must come down first.

extraProducts.description:
The extra products they can buy now, or null when they cannot: no running
tier, or buying them would still leave fewer places than products
published.

message.description: A sentence the app may show as it is. No em-dash.

stage.description:
Where the check stands: `needs_documents` (the documents the bank asked
for are still needed), `rejected`, `stopped` (for good) or `expired`
(left unfinished too long). The same words as `review.stage` on
`GET /money/wallet`.

message.description: The Hub's sentence: what is paused, why, and what to do. The app shows it as it is. No em-dash.

key.description: The `key` or the `fileUrl` POST /uploads/presign returned for this file.

amount.description:
Naira, whole numbers only. The ₦50 floor keeps obviously-bogus charges out;
the ceiling is a blast radius limit, not a product rule.

refundReference.description:
The provider/bank reference for the refund that was actually sent. Not
optional, on purpose.

password.description:
Capped because argon2 hashes whatever it is given: an unbounded password
field is a cheap way to make the server do expensive work.

phoneNumber.description: Nigerian mobile number. WellaHealth keys the enrollee on this.

body.description:
Bounded at both ends. A minimum because an empty turn burns a model call
and tells the consultant nothing; a maximum because this is a chat box,
and somebody pasting a whole contract into it should attach the document
instead — where the consultant can actually open it.
What the client typed. At most 2000 characters.

quickReplyId.description: The `id` of one of the thread's live `quickReplies`.

details.description: Whatever the service's intake form collected.

scheduledFor.description:
The slot the client picked, from GET /legal/availability. Required for
chat and Zoom; physical consultations are arranged directly and book no
slot, so it is optional here and rejected in the service for physical.

fullName.description:
The signer types their own full name. This is the signature: it is stored
with the exact contract text and a timestamp.

notes.description: What was discussed. Kept so the quote that follows has a basis.

priceKobo.description:
The price in kobo, whole naira only (a multiple of 100), or null to leave
the kind unpriced so the app does not offer it. Always null for an
in-person consultation.

minutes.description: How long it runs, in minutes, or null to leave the kind unset. Null for in person.

enabled.description: Switch the kind off without losing its price. Defaults to on.

priceKobo.description: The price in kobo, whole naira only, or null to quote the service instead.

fileName.description: What the file is called in the chat and on the delivery screen.

url.description:
The file's `fileUrl` or `key` from POST /uploads/presign: a link on WAWU
storage or a bare key, under `legal/document/`, uploaded by the client
this request belongs to or by one of the legal team's accounts
(`LEGAL_DELIVERY_UPLOADER_IDS`). Anything else, including another
client's document and a key nobody uploaded, is refused with a 400 naming
this field (N1, FIX-24).

pages.description: Page count, when it is known.

reason.description:
Required, and required to be substantial. The applicant sees this and has
to be able to act on it — "rejected" on its own turns a review into a
dead end and generates a support ticket instead of a resubmission.

category.description:
Must be one of the 25 taxonomy ids (src/common/categories.ts). A free
string here let content be filed under a category no browse surface
lists, which made it unreachable.

specializations.description:
Specialization ids from the C1 taxonomy, e.g.
`photography.portrait-photographer`. What a buyer actually searches and
filters on; `category` above is the deprecated flat list it replaces.

Optional and capped at three rather than required, deliberately:
 - optional, because every piece published before this column exists has
   none, and a required field would make those rows unrepublishable.
 - capped, because this drives search placement. A piece tagged with
   twenty specializations is tagged with none, and the cap belongs here
   as well as in the client: a client-side maximum is a suggestion.

The ids are NOT validated against the taxonomy here. That list lives in
the web client and changes by deploy, so pinning a copy in this DTO would
create two lists that drift and reject valid input the day they diverge.
Shape is enforced; membership is the client's to get right.

parentCourseId.description:
FIX-111 (H24): the creator's own course this piece comes from ("From the course VFX for Beginners"). Optional, and only for a
piece that is not itself a course; the course must be the creator's, live or in review. Stored on the piece's side row.

specializations.description: Replaces the whole list, as on create (at most three).

tags.description: Replaces the whole list, as on create (at most twenty).

frames.description:
The pictures of a photo set, in the order they are shown. Replaces the
whole list. Photo sets only (content type `image`).

durationLabel.description: How long a video, audio or course runs, as `4:12` or `1:20:05`.

pageCount.description: How many pages a PDF has. PDFs only.

id.description: An existing lesson of this course to keep (its progress and place stay); left out, a new lesson is made.

durationLabel.description: The lesson's length as a player writes it: `4:12` or `1:20:05`.

assetKey.description:
The lesson's file: the key (or link) of an upload this person made under `content/full`. A new lesson with none has no file yet.
A lesson kept by `id` keeps the file it has when this is left out (FIX-111: the editor does not know the key of a file it did not
upload), takes a new one when a key is sent, and loses its file only when this is `null`.

specializations.description: At most three, as on POST /content.

tags.description: At most twenty, as on POST /content.

mediaJobId.description:
The AI tool job whose audio this product uses (AITOOLS-07): one of the
caller's own finished jobs, or `null` to detach it. Optional; a draft
without it behaves exactly as before.

The AI tool job whose audio this product uses (AITOOLS-07): one of the
caller's own finished jobs, or `null` to detach it. Optional; a draft
without it behaves exactly as before.

documents.description:
Object-storage URLs for the supporting documents (valid ID, signature,
passport photograph), uploaded via POST /uploads/presign before this
call. Optional so existing clients keep working.

note.description: What the applicant wants. Free text, because each partner asks differently.

documents.description:
Object-storage URLs for the CAC certificate, product sample photos and
bank reference letter the applicant uploads before this call.

The NEPC apply screen makes all three mandatory and blocks the submit
button until every one has finished uploading — and then sent none of
them, because this DTO had no field for them and the global
ValidationPipe runs `forbidNonWhitelisted`. Every applicant's documents
were being uploaded to object storage and then orphaned. Optional so the
currently-shipped client, which still omits them, keeps working.

label.description: The timeline entry's heading, e.g. "Under review", "Names checked".

status.description:
Free-form because the column is a plain String and the shipped client
maps four known values (`under_review`, `approved`, `rejected`,
`pending`) with a fallback — constraining it to an enum here would break
intake's own `awaiting_payment` and `submitted`.

reason.description:
Why it was refused. Shown to the applicant verbatim, so it is required
and has to say something: a rejection with no reason is the dead end
this endpoint exists to end.

certificateUrl.description:
The issued certificate, uploaded via POST /uploads/presign. Appended to
the existing `documents` array rather than given a column of its own:
ServiceApplication is one of the bare Prisma re-exports returned by
spread, so a new column would silently widen a live app response.

trackingNote.description: "Sent via GIG, waybill 12345." Free text, because there is no API here.

priceNaira.description:
Naira. Zero is allowed — a `free` tier is a real thing — but the service
refuses a zero price on a paid tier, because a "VIP" ticket costing
nothing is a mistake somebody will only notice after it sells out.

quantity.description: No unlimited option: a venue has a capacity and somebody must state it.

priceMinor.description: Whole minor units of the reason's `currency` (kobo or cents).

code.description:
`tier_required`, or `account_type_required` for an account that is
neither a creator nor a professional (it carries no tier fields).

tierState.description: `none` (never had a tier) or `ended`. Only on `tier_required`.

currency.description:
The currency of `lowestTier.priceMinor`. Absent only when the Hub could
not read the plan at that moment; the app then shows `message` alone.

steps.description: What to do, in order. Only on `account_type_required`.

purchasable.description:
Kept from the verification refusal this answer replaces so no reader of
it breaks: always empty. Only on `account_type_required`.

message.description: A sentence the app may show as it is. No em-dash.

referralCode.description: The referral link this buyer arrived through, when there was one.

reason.description:
Required, and shown to every ticket holder. Somebody who has bought a
ticket and arranged their day around it is owed a sentence, not a status
change.

handle.description: With or without the "@". Same characters a handle may hold.

balanceKobo.description: insufficient_funds: the wallet provider's available balance when the movement was refused.

totalKobo.description: insufficient_funds, daily_limit_exceeded: the total the request needed (amount plus fees).

shortfallKobo.description: insufficient_funds: totalKobo minus balanceKobo, what to add before trying again.

remainingTodayKobo.description: daily_limit_exceeded, limit_reached: what is left of today's limit.

limitKobo.description: limit_reached on the account's daily limit (WALLET-23): the limit itself, in kobo.

feeQuote.description: quote_changed on a transfer: the quote as it stands now.

paymentQuote.description: quote_changed on a payment: the quote as it stands now.

pointsQuote.description: quote_changed on a points conversion: the quote as it stands now, with a new token.

limit.description: limit_reached: which limit the movement passes (NUV-07), WAWU's own or the provider's.

minimumPoints.description: below_minimum: the fewest points one conversion to cash takes (POINTS-04).

balancePoints.description: below_minimum, insufficient_points: the points the person has now.

cap.description: points_cap_reached (POINTS-03): which cap stopped the job.

usedPoints.description: points_cap_reached, daily cap: points of AI jobs held or spent today.

remainingPoints.description: points_cap_reached, daily cap: points still free today.

resetsAt.description: points_cap_reached, daily cap: when the day's count starts again (ISO 8601).

message.description: A sentence the app may show as it is. Never an em-dash, never a provider's raw text.

triesLeft.description: pin_incorrect: wrong tries left before the PIN locks. reset_code_invalid: tries left on this code.

lockedUntil.description: pin_locked: when the lock ends, ISO 8601 UTC.

paymentId.description: payment_in_progress: the payment for this item still being confirmed (MONEY-17).

accountName.description:
account_name_changed: the name the bank gives for the account now (the
name to show for the person to confirm), and the bank's name for it.

verifiedName.description:
account_not_in_your_name: the name on the person's wallet, set beside
`accountName` (the bank's name for the account) and `bankName`. Left out
when the wallet holds no name to show. The comparison itself is made on
the verified name's keyed hashes, never on this text (WALLET-37).

retryAfterSeconds.description: provider_unreachable, idempotency_in_progress, identity_checks_exhausted, open_address_limited, selfie_checks_exhausted, reset_codes_exhausted, recipient_search_rate_limited, name_check_rate_limited: seconds to wait before trying again.

checksLeft.description: bvn_not_confirmed, bvn_phone_mismatch: BVN checks left in the current 24 hours. selfie_not_matched: selfie matches left in the current 24 hours.

pinConfirmation.description: The second entry (A10 "Enter it again"). A difference is `pin_mismatch`.

code.description: The code from the text message. Its length is set by whoever sends it (MONEY-14).

publicKey.description:
The public half of a P-256 key the phone made, as SubjectPublicKeyInfo
(DER), base64url without padding. Its private half stays on the phone,
unlocked only by the phone's biometric.

biometric.description: What the phone approves with, for W35's label.

bvn.description: The Bank Verification Number: 11 digits, no spaces.

nin.description: The National Identification Number: 11 digits, no spaces. Fintava needs it to open the account.

bvn.description:
The BVN whose check passed: 11 digits, no spaces. Leave it out and send
`checkHandle` instead (KYC-03); one of the two, never both.

checkHandle.description:
The `checkHandle` the passed BVN check answered, in place of `bvn`
(KYC-03): the server takes the BVN from it. One of the two, never both.

image.description:
The selfie: plain base64 (no `data:` prefix) of a JPEG or PNG, 1 KB to
about 75 KB (at most 100,000 base64 characters), at most 2,048 pixels
on each side. A face match against the BVN photo, not a liveness check.

occupation.description: 2 to 80 characters with at least one letter; spaces at either end are dropped.

bvn.description:
The BVN whose check passed: 11 digits, no spaces. Leave it and `nin` out
and send `checkHandle` instead (KYC-03); never both.

nin.description: The NIN given with that check: 11 digits, no spaces. Left out with `checkHandle`.

checkHandle.description:
The `checkHandle` the passed BVN check answered, in place of `bvn` and
`nin` (KYC-03): the server takes both from it. Never with them.

addressLine2.description: A second address line (flat, estate), when there is one.

postalCode.description: The postal code, 1 to 20 letters, digits, spaces or dashes.

idType.description: The ID document the person will upload (NUV-03).

idNumber.description: Its number, as printed: 5 to 30 letters, digits or dashes. Never stored.

idIssueDate.description: When it was issued, `YYYY-MM-DD`, when it says.

idExpiryDate.description: When it expires, `YYYY-MM-DD`, when it says; not already passed.

proofOfAddressType.description: The proof of address the person will upload (NUV-03).

firstName.description: A5's first name, as the BVN check prefilled it.

lastName.description: A5's last name, as the BVN check prefilled it.

address.description:
The full home address in one line (street, town, state), 5 to 200
characters with a letter in it. Fintava takes it as one field.

confirmCurrentName.description:
bank_account only (WALLET-09): the person has seen the bank and the name
the bank gives for this saved account now (`409 account_name_changed`)
and confirms them. The server asks the bank and keeps what it says, in
place of the name kept before. Left out, saving an account already saved
answers the row as it is, as it always did.

from.description: The first day of the statement, YYYY-MM-DD in Africa/Lagos time, included.

to.description:
The last day of the statement, YYYY-MM-DD in Africa/Lagos time,
included. On or after `from`, not after today in Lagos, and at most
366 days from `from`, both days counted (STATEMENT_MAX_DAYS).

format.description:
The file. Only `csv` today: Fintava issues no stamped statement
(WALLET-27, BACKEND_GAPS G-68), so there is no `pdf`.

amountKobo.description: Only for a tip. Every other price is the server's own record of the item.

expectedTotalKobo.description: `totalKobo` from the payment quote the person saw. A different server total is `quote_changed`.

quoteToken.description:
`quoteToken` from that payment quote (MONEY-17, BACKEND_GAPS G-64): the
server checks it is its own, for this person and this price, and not
past `expiresAt`; otherwise `409 quote_changed` with the new quote.

note.description: Only for a tip: the message that goes with it, 500 characters as POST /tips takes today.

amountKobo.description: What the recipient gets, in kobo.

expectedTotalKobo.description: `totalKobo` from the fee quote the person saw. A different server total is `quote_changed`.

quoteToken.description:
`quoteToken` from that fee quote (`GET /money/fees/quote?kind=
wawu_transfer`; BACKEND_GAPS G-64): the server checks it is its own, for
this person and this amount, and not past `expiresAt`; otherwise `409
quote_changed` with the new quote.

note.description: W9's optional note, 100 characters at most.

amountKobo.description: What the bank account gets, in kobo.

expectedTotalKobo.description: `totalKobo` from the fee quote the person saw. A different server total is `quote_changed`.

quoteToken.description:
`quoteToken` from that fee quote (`GET /money/fees/quote?kind=
bank_transfer`; BACKEND_GAPS G-64): the server checks it is its own, for
this person and this amount, and not past `expiresAt`; otherwise `409
quote_changed` with the new quote.

nameToken.description:
`nameToken` from the name check the person saw (`POST
/money/banks/name-check`). Required for an account that is not saved
(WALLET-09 round 2, FIX-41): the send is bound to the holder's name they
were shown, and a send without it is a `400` with nothing sent. If the
bank names another holder now, the answer is `409 account_name_changed`
and nothing is sent. A saved account (a beneficiary, or the payout
account) is compared with its kept name and ignores it.

note.description: W9's optional note, 100 characters at most.

message.description: A sentence about the first field that is wrong.

redirectUrl.description:
Where the secure selfie page sends the person when it is done: a secure
(https) web address, the app's link or the website. Optional.

clientMessageId.description:
The dashboard's own id for this reply. Sending the same one again returns
the reply already stored instead of posting it twice.

key.description: The `key` POST /chats/:chatId/attachments returned, after the upload.

name.description: The file's own name, shown on a PDF bubble.

clientMessageId.description:
The app's own id for this message. Sending the same one again returns
the message already stored instead of posting it twice.

contentType.description: image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, video/mp4, video/quicktime or application/pdf.

contentLength.description:
Exact size in bytes; the upload link is signed for this length. Up to
512 MB, the limit every upload already has (MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES).

imageUrl.description:
The picture. Optional: an announcement with nothing to show renders as
the compact row, which is better than a stock photograph chosen to fill a
frame.

actionLabel.description:
Button label and destination. BOTH or NEITHER, enforced in the service:
a label with no destination is a dead control, and a destination with no
label is unreachable.

actionHref.description: Checked against CAMPAIGN_DESTINATIONS in the service, which is the allowlist.

version.description: The version the editor loaded. A save over a newer one is refused.

reason.description: Why the person is leaving; left out when they did not say.

blockers.description: What to settle first. The app leads with `wallet_balance` (Withdraw).

balanceKobo.description: The wallet provider's balance in kobo, when the person has a wallet.

openHolds.description: Holds open for or against the person (paid DMs, tickets, bills).

waitingEarnings.description: Sales whose share has not reached the person's wallet yet.

message.description: A sentence the app may show as it is.

expoPushToken.description: The phone's Expo push token, `ExponentPushToken[...]` or `ExpoPushToken[...]`, exactly as the app got it.

deviceId.description: The phone's own id, if the app has one.

deviceLabel.description: A name for the phone ("Pixel 8"), if the app has one.

city.description: Where you work, as people will read it: "Ikeja", "Port Harcourt".

until.description: ISO 8601. Omit for a tick that does not expire.

moneyIn.description: Tips and sales (SETTINGS-07). Optional; absent leaves it as it is.

contentReviews.description: An upload approved or sent back (SETTINGS-07). Optional; absent leaves it as it is.

communityMessages.description: Community messages (SETTINGS-07). Optional; absent leaves it as it is. Stored only: nothing sends that kind yet.

show.description: false stops the daily TGIF notification for this account; true sends one each morning (HOME-16, R-59).

firstName.description:
The three name parts.

Names are WAWU ID's, not this service's, so these are PROXIED there
rather than stored here. They live on this DTO because the profile screen
is where somebody edits their name, and making them save it through a
second endpoint would be an implementation detail leaking into a form.

All three move together: a partial update would let a surname change
land while a first name failed.

headline.description:
The one line under the name. A person's own sentence about what they do,
not a category: see the schema note on why the first interest was the
wrong thing to render there.

company.description:
The organisation this person is part of, beside the location and the
website on the profile header.

Free text and no @IsUrl: it is a name, not a link. See the schema's note
on why it is not a relation to an Organisation row.

avatarUrl.description:
Both come from POST /uploads/presign, so they are our own storage URLs
rather than anything a client composes. @IsUrl keeps a malformed value out
of a field the profile header renders directly.

THE LENGTH CAP IS 2048, NOT 500. A presigned S3 URL carries the signature,
the credential scope, the expiry and the signed-header list in its query
string: a real one measured 541 characters. At 500 this endpoint rejected
every avatar and cover with "must be shorter than or equal to 500
characters", so the image uploaded and then the save failed - which is
exactly how it was reported.

2048 is the conventional ceiling for a URL and leaves room for a longer
key or an extra signed header without landing back here.

location.description: Where the person is, free text ("Lagos, Nigeria"). null or "" clears it.

skills.description: Skills and expertise chips. [] clears them.

openTo.description: What the person is open to, as chips. [] clears them.

threadsHandle.description: Threads handle, with or without the "@". null or "" clears it.

socialOrder.description:
The order the social links show in, first to last, as platform keys. Each
key once. [] puts them back in the default order.

endedOn.description:
Omitted or null means this is the role they hold now.

There is no `current` flag to send alongside it, for the reason the
schema gives: two fields that can contradict each other eventually do.

media.description:
The keys (or the `fileUrl`s) `POST /uploads/presign` returned for the
`profile/work` folder, first one the cover. Each must be this person's
own upload; anything else is a 400.
The whole list, replaced. [] clears it.

endYear.description: Omitted or null means still studying there.

handle.description: The username, with or without a leading "@". Checked by `checkHandleShape`; its words are the server's.
The username, with or without a leading "@". Checked by `checkHandleShape`; its words are the server's.

intakeId.description: The intake to hold a place in. The course and school come from it.

nextIntake.description: class_full: the soonest other class of the course that has a seat and has not started; null when there is none (SC11).

enrolmentId.description: already_enrolled: the enrolment the student already has in this course.

message.description: A sentence the app may show as it is.

passPriceKobo.description:
What a member pays for 30 days, in kobo, set by the host (I32). Private
rooms only. The bounds are checked by the service (a figure of the
launch settings, COMMUNITY_PASS_MIN_KOBO and COMMUNITY_PASS_MAX_KOBO).
A private room must carry it (there is no host approval step, R-63):
left out, the answer is 400 "A private room needs a monthly price.".

name.description:
Bound: 3-80 characters. A community name is a list-row heading on both
the mobile and desktop community surfaces, so it is deliberately far
shorter than ContentPiece.title (200) — anything longer is a
description, not a name. `\S` rejects an all-whitespace name, which
@IsNotEmpty alone lets through and which renders as a blank, unclickable
row.

description.description:
Bound: 1-500 characters. This is the "what this community is for" blurb
shown on the community card / join screen, not long-form content — an
order of magnitude shorter than ContentPiece.description (5000), which
backs a full detail page. Required, because `Community.description` is
a non-nullable column and a community with no stated purpose is the
